deep.reconstruction:
Setting: X → S, Mod(X/S) is the category whose objects are O_X-modules (perhaps quasi-coherent) and whose morphisms are differential operators rel S of bounded order. P^i denotes the (pro-)ring of principal parts of the infinitesimal neighbourhoods of the diagonal in X^{i+1}; these form a cosimplicial ring P^*. On the previous page the modules Q^i[M] = Q^i ⊗_{O_X} M are assembled into a cosimplicial module Q^*[M] over P^*. The key observation there is that its components are obtained from one another by base change along the cosimplicial maps P^i → P^j, i.e. Q^*[M] is cartesian ('les objets d'une lim').

This page draws the consequence. A cartesian cosimplicial module over P^* is the same as its degree-0 term together with descent / stratification data. So, formally (up to working with complete pro-modules instead of modules), Q^0[M] = P^∞_{X/S} ⊗ M is a pro-module on X with a stratification rel S. The higher Q^i[M] are the components of the associated cosimplicial object, a Čech–Alexander or linearized de Rham type complex.

The functor M ↦ Q^0[M], from Mod(X/S) to stratified pro-modules, is apparently claimed to be fully faithful. Its essential image is a category of pro-objects (marginal note: 'de parties principales') that are coherent in the sense of Artin–Rees.

Full faithfulness is the standard fact
Hom_strat(P(M), P(N)) = Hom_{O_X}(P(M), N) = colim_n Hom_{O_X}(P^n ⊗ M, N) = Diff(M, N).
This is why bounded order is needed. Finally, M is recovered from Q^0[M] as the subsheaf of special sections. These are most plausibly the horizontal sections: m ↦ 1 ⊗ m is horizontal for the canonical stratification. The next page confirms that a differential operator D is recovered from the O_X-linear map Q^0[D] induced on these sections. This is Grothendieck's 'linearization of differential operators', the device that converts differential operators into linear maps of crystals or stratified modules. It is used to build the linearized de Rham complex in crystalline cohomology.
errors: No mathematical error is visible. The full-faithfulness statement needs differential operators of bounded order, which the page explicitly imposes, and it needs Hom in the pro-category; Grothendieck flags both caveats ('pro-Modules au lieu de Modules et complets').
The characterization of the essential image ('cohérent au sens d'Artin-Rees') is only sketched and its precise hypotheses are not legible.

ideas.what: Cosimplicial module Q^*[M] over the cosimplicial ring of principal parts is cartesian; its degree-0 term P^∞⊗M is a stratified pro-module
ideas.modern_name: Linearization L(M) = P^∞_{X/S} ⊗ M as a crystal / stratified module; Čech–Alexander cosimplicial description
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Crystals and de Rham cohomology, 1968); Berthelot (1974); Berthelot–Ogus
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck, 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes', Dix exposés (1968), section on linearization of differential operators

ideas.what: Full faithfulness of M ↦ P^∞⊗M from (modules, differential operators of bounded order) to stratified pro-modules; D recovered from the linear map it induces
ideas.modern_name: Linearization of differential operators: Diff(M,N) = Hom_crys(L(M), L(N))
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck; Berthelot–Ogus, Notes on crystalline cohomology
ideas.where_published: Dix exposés (Crystals, 1968); EGA IV §16 for principal parts and differential operators

ideas.what: Essential image described as pro-objects coherent in the Artin–Rees sense; M recovered as the subsheaf of horizontal (special) sections
ideas.modern_name: Characterization of induced / linearized stratified pro-modules; Artin–Rees pro-category
ideas.usually_credited_to: unsure; the pro-category viewpoint is close to Deligne/Hartshorne-style pro-coherent formalisms

missed.claim: An intrinsic characterization of the essential image of the linearization functor inside stratified pro-modules, via Artin–Rees coherence of pro-objects. This is only sketched here; published accounts use linearization without characterizing its image.
missed.quote: de pro-objets [?] ... premier [?] cohérent [?] au sens de Artin-Rees
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It would give an equivalence 'differential operators = linear maps between a specified class of crystals'. Such a statement is relevant to D-module / crystal dualities and to derived treatments of crystalline and de Rham cohomology. However, it is likely implicitly known to specialists.

deep.surprise_reason: This is mainly the standard linearization of differential operators (published by Grothendieck in 1968 and developed by Berthelot). The only less-standard detail is the Artin–Rees characterization of the essential image, which is too sketchy and illegible to count as a clear missed result.
transcription_corrections: 'qc [?] diff.' should read '[Modules sur X ou op. diff. rel S d'ordre borné]': morphisms are differential operators rel S of bounded order.
In 'Q^0[M]' vs 'O^0[M]', the symbol is the same Q (principal parts tensor M) used on the previous page.
In 'sections Artiniennes [?]', the underlined word is uncertain; mathematically 'sections horizontales' (or a similar word for invariant sections) is expected.
Marginal insertion reads 'des parties principales', attached to 'correspondant'.
